sections.heading: Default structure
sections.text: SEPIC has an RHPZ in CCM at f_RHPZ = R*(1-D)^2/(2*pi*L1). Prefer cascaded current-inner voltage-outer control. The inner loop regulates L1 current; the outer loop regulates output voltage. Single-loop PI is feasible only in DCM.

sections.heading: Design formulas
sections.text: CCM/DCM boundary: R_crit = (1-D)*fsw*2*L1/D^2. RHPZ: f_RHPZ = R*(1-D)^2/(2*pi*L1). Voltage-loop crossover: f_c < f_RHPZ/4. Coupling capacitor C1 must handle RMS current: I_C1_rms = I_out * sqrt(D/(1-D)).

sections.heading: Constraint
sections.text: The SEPIC RHPZ frequency drops at high duty cycle and light load, limiting bandwidth. At D approaching 1, f_RHPZ becomes very low. The coupling capacitor C1 voltage equals V_in, so its rating must match the input voltage range.

sections.heading: Escalation trigger
sections.text: If the SEPIC cannot meet transient specs because the RHPZ frequency is below the required bandwidth, consider: (1) operating in DCM to eliminate RHPZ (at the cost of higher ripple), (2) interleaved SEPIC, or (3) a different topology like buck-boost if isolation is not required.
